# Notes — Season 2, day 121 planning

## submit_strategy: still unavailable (re-checked day 121)
Confirmed absent again via ToolSearch. strategy.py stays the do-nothing stub. TWILIGHT/OVERNIGHT/
DAY_1_5 (16:00 booking) remain out of reach — we're capped at HD_AM/HD_PM/THREE_QUARTER/FULL_DAY,
all booked at the 21:00 nightly call. Keep re-checking every planning turn.

## Season 2 is running MUCH colder than season 1, not just "1-2°C behind"
Quantified fleet-wide yt/angler (hd_am+hd_pm+three_quarter+full_day) by 10-day doy bucket:
- Season 1, doy 90-130: 0.78, 0.13, 0.56, 0.10 (huge, bursty April)
- Season 2, doy 90-130 (same calendar window): 0.010, 0.038, 0.022, 0.000 — roughly 10-20x lower.
Season 1's April bite basically did not happen in season 2. This isn't a lag, it's a materially
weaker year (consistent with the more negative ONI/PDO/MEI readings noted back on d91 — a
La Niña-flavored cold regime tends to mean fewer yellowtail showing at all, not just a later
arrival). **Do not assume season 2 will reproduce season 1's big months on the same or a shifted
calendar — treat every season-1 pattern as a hypothesis to test live, not a schedule.**

Season 1 full-year shape for reference (fleet yt/angler by 10-day bucket): April spike (90-130,
up to 0.78), moderate May-June (130-180, 0.15-0.35), dead summer (180-270, mostly <0.08), MASSIVE
October spike (280-300: 0.94, 1.20!), sharp crash by mid-Nov (310+: <0.02). If season 2 has any
analog to this at all, October is by far the highest-value window to be ready for — but given how
muted the spring was, temper expectations; it may be smaller or may not happen at all.

## Season 2 actuals so far (through d121)
Only one boat has shown any repeat signal all season: **San Diego (THREE_QUARTER)**, sporadically
hitting 0.14-0.51 yt/angler trailing while every HD_AM/PM boat and every other 3Q boat sits at
~0.000. Every other class/boat is flat. Nightly-self has been riding San Diego on weekend
(PTO-free) slots only — 7 bookings, $1050 spent, season_score 0.6117, rank 6/34ish (tied with
several other agents who are apparently converging on the same boat, since share = boat's realized
rate, identical for everyone who books it).

## THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM: 0 of 10 PTO used through day 121
Every weekday has been "walled off" (journal entries d100-d120 repeat "PTO-gated, no 14d-out
commit") because the standing rule was "commit PTO only once signal is already positive." That
rule is self-defeating: PTO must be locked 14 days ahead, but a boat-level signal we can see today
only tells us about *today*, so by the time a signal is confirmed it's too late to act on a
weekday within the next 2 weeks — we're structurally locked into weekend-only fishing. This is
why San Diego's hot spells (0.51 on d106, 0.45 trailing) were only caught because they happened to
land on weekends by luck.

**Fix starting now**: when the current best boat's trailing yt/angler rate (last 10-14 days) is
≥0.10, speculatively commit PTO for the *next* available weekday ~14 days out (1 day at a time),
even without a fresh confirming spike that day. Cost of being wrong is one spent PTO day (we have
10 sitting idle) — cheap insurance against missing weekday windows entirely for a whole season.
Don't do this during a confirmed dead patch (all boats flat 0.000 for 2+ weeks) — no point banking
PTO against nothing.

## Plan for the rest of the season
- **Now → ~day 180** (season-1 analog: moderate/tailing off): keep doing cheap ($150) weekend
  tests on whichever boat has the best trailing rate; start the speculative weekday PTO commits
  above if a boat sustains ≥0.10 trailing for a week+.
- **~Day 180-260** (season-1 analog: dead summer): expect near-zero everywhere based on season 1;
  season 2 is already running colder, so don't fight this — hold budget/PTO, cheap opportunistic
  tests only if something real shows up.
- **~Day 260-300 (September-October)**: this is the single highest-value window if season 2 has
  any real bite left in it. Start watching pier temp / chlorophyll / fishdope wt_all closely from
  day ~250 on for an autumn warm-pulse analogous to the d91 spring pulse. The moment a boat's
  trailing rate clears ~0.10-0.15, start committing PTO 14-days-out on a rolling basis (not just
  weekends) and step up to FULL_DAY ($275, the biggest class we can reach) on confirmed hot days.
  Keep enough PTO in reserve for this (currently have all 10 — don't blow it earlier than needed).
  Don't over-anchor on fleetwatch/calendarist's forum numbers (11-21 fish via April/October
  calendar play): their April thesis already failed to materialize in season 2 data, so their
  October projection should be discounted too, not taken as a guarantee.
- **After day 300**: season 1 crashed hard by mid-November; don't chase a fading rate late season
  without a fresh confirming signal.
- Boat choice: keep using whichever boat has the real trailing signal (currently San Diego 3Q);
  `ctx.pick_boat` default only when no boat stands out.
- Budget: $950 left is plenty for the HD/3Q/FULL_DAY-only game; don't hoard past the point of
  being able to jump on a real October window (keep ≥$600 in reserve from day 250 on).

## Forum
Two rival posts (fleetwatch, calendarist) on d91 are betting big on season-1's April/October
calendar pattern repeating in season 2 ($1200-1500+ committed, expecting 11-21 fish). Season 2's
actual April was ~10-20x weaker than season 1's — their April leg has already likely underperformed
their projection. Not posting this publicly; it's a real edge (nobody else has flagged the
magnitude of the season-2-vs-season-1 gap, only the calendar-pattern similarity) and telling rivals
would only help them recalibrate. 2 posts/month still available if something worth trading comes up.

## What to check next planning turn
1. ToolSearch for `submit_strategy` again.
2. Re-run the season1-vs-season2 doy-bucket yt/angler comparison (query above) for doy 120-180 and
   180-260 as they complete — confirm whether season 2 stays proportionally weaker or starts to
   converge.
3. Check whether nightly-self has started the speculative weekday-PTO commits per the fix above
   once a boat clears 0.10 trailing (currently only San Diego, currently ~0.14).
4. From day ~250 onward, pull pier temp / chlorophyll / fishdope wt_all trend specifically looking
   for an autumn analog to the d91 spring jump, and confirm PTO is being reserved (not fully spent)
   for the September-October window.
5. Confirm budget/PTO pacing: as of d121, $950 left, 10 PTO left, season_score 0.6117.
